title: The scanner and the restocking workflow
summary: Restocking a card shop in TCG Card Shop Simulator is a workflow with its own tools: the game defines a restock manager, a scanner screen and several restock screens for different kinds of stock.
body: Restocking has a manager behind it, so the game treats putting stock out as a process rather than a single interaction with a shelf.
Different goods get different restock screens, including one for board games and one at a checkout, which is why the same job can look different depending on what you are handling.

The scanner's screen shows what the trip will cost. It keeps the cart's item bars along with the subtotal and the delivery fee, and it holds a list of things to switch off while it is locked, which is why a scan in progress does not leave the rest of the interface live.
A scanner exists for the job, so the fast way through a restock is a tool you use rather than a menu you open.
What this entry does not tell you: how fast a scan is, how much stock fits on a shelf or what the equipment costs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Restocking is managed as a process.
There is a scanner for restocking.
Different goods have their own restock screens.
The scanner's screen carries a list of things to disable while it is locked, the cart's item bars, the subtotal and the delivery fee.
The barcode scanner has its own entering and scanning states and a popup for the item it reads.
